title: Quenched Polish Sauerkraut Pierogi
description: A festive Polish dish featuring gochugaru-spiced sauerkraut, served in a rich, creamy mustardy sauce, with a molten, cheesy center.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine cauliflower flour, sauerkraut, gochugaru, salt, and pepper; mix well.
Add the egg and mix until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 12 equal pieces and roll each piece into a ball.
Flatten each ball of dough into a thin circle.
Place a tablespoon of the sauerkraut mixture in the center of each circle.
Fold the dough over the filling, forming a half-circle shape, and press the edges together to seal.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the pierogi to the skillet and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until they are golden brown.
Transfer the pierogi to a baking dish and top with the remaining sauerkraut mixture, Grana Padano cheese, and heavy cream.
Bake in a preheated oven at 375°F for 15-20 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve hot.
